root_cause.text: Two KVM/arm64 functions, __kvm_at_s12() and __kvm_find_s1_desc_level(), invoke page table walkers (kvm_walk_nested_s2() and walk_s1()) without holding the required kvm->srcu lock, violating the lock contract needed to protect against concurrent memslot modifications.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "walk_s1() and kvm_walk_nested_s2() expect to be called while holding kvm->srcu to guard against memslot changes. While this is generally the case, __kvm_at_s12() and __kvm_find_s1_desc_level() call into the respective walkers without taking kvm->srcu." The patch adds `scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu)` before each problematic call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Acquire SRCU lock before calling kvm_walk_nested_s2 to prevent race conditions.
intent_record.what: Wrapped the call to kvm_walk_nested_s2 in a scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu) to acquire SRCU read-side lock.
intent_record.how: Ensures that the nested stage-2 translation operation is protected by the VM's SRCU lock, preventing concurrent access to freed or modified data structures.

intent_record.intent_summary: Wrap walk_s1 call with SRCU read-side critical section to prevent data races during S1 page table walk in KVM.
intent_record.what: Added scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu) around the call to walk_s1, moving the assignment inside the guarded block.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that the walk_s1 function is executed while holding an SRCU read lock on the KVM instance, preventing concurrent modifications to the page tables from causing data races or use-after-free errors.

grouping_result.intent: Wrap walk_s1 call with SRCU read-side critical section to prevent data races during S1 page table walk in KVM.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add SRCU read-side critical sections to protect nested page table walks in KVM from data races.

relevance_review.reason: Group 0 directly adds SRCU read-side critical sections around the page table walk functions (kvm_walk_nested_s2 and walk_s1), which precisely addresses the root cause of missing kvm->srcu lock in __kvm_at_s12() and __kvm_find_s1_desc_level().

candidates.rationale: This function call performs a stage-2 translation walk without holding the kvm->srcu lock, which can lead to data races when memslots are concurrently modified.
This function call performs a stage-1 page table walk without holding the kvm->srcu lock, violating the required lock contract to protect against concurrent memslot modifications.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement calls kvm_walk_nested_s2() without holding the kvm->srcu lock, violating the lock contract needed to protect against concurrent memslot modifications, leading to potential data races.
This statement calls walk_s1() without holding the kvm->srcu lock, violating the required lock contract to protect against concurrent memslot modifications during stage-1 page table walk.
